reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology combines Bayesian mixed-effects modeling with Monte Carlo simulation to infer true team strength from noisy game data. The model treats each game event as a draw from a Poisson process, with log-link function to ensure positivity of expected goals. Random effects for team and opponent allow for partial pooling, stabilizing estimates for teams with sparse data. Phase-specific modeling accounts for varying game states (even-strength, power-play, penalty-kill) and venue effects (home/away). Back-transformed estimates are weighted by actual time-on-ice to yield composite strength metrics. These are then used in Monte Carlo simulations to generate win probabilities for tournament matchups. The approach addresses the fundamental flaw of traditional metrics by incorporating context (opponent quality, game state) and generating probabilistic forecasts rather than deterministic rankings.
